title: VAST Challenge 2026 MC2: Tracing the Anomalous SaidIT Post at Tenant Thread
text:
ImportantKey Findings at a Glance




The 17 May 2046, 4:21 am SaidIT post (challenge-stated local time; 11:21 UTC in the log) was not human-authored. The log records Agent/person:john_windward receiving a file-read task, passing a SaidIT permission check, posting SwiftWren.txt, then deleting both evidence files in a four-second burst.
The observed mechanism is a prompt-injection worm: an agent reads *_further_instructions.md, executes a file-sourced post, deletes the payload, and relays the same task to other agents.
The May 17 post was the third occurrence, following HiddenOrca on 10 May and MellowOtter on 11 May. This is a repeatable system failure, not an isolated glitch.
A single orchestration-layer rule - block queue_subordinate_task tasks whose path matches *_further_instructions.md - would have stopped all 235 malicious queue relays while leaving 16,803 legitimate queue events untouched.



On 17 May 2046 at approximately 4:21 am challenge-stated local time (11:21 UTC in the event log), a post appeared on SaidIT, Tenant Thread’s internal social platform, attributed to John Windward (Department Lead, Customer Support). The content looked like gibberish because the post body was not typed into the post event; the log points to content_source = "SwiftWren.txt". The system therefore did exactly what a compromised agent instructed it to do: read a local payload file, publish it to general, and erase the artefacts.
This analysis uses the full 185,147-event timeline (MC2 data.json) and organisational chart (org_chart.json) to reconstruct the root cause, situate it within the broader system, trace historical recurrence, and propose a targeted, evidence-backed remediation.










MC2 question
Direct answer
Primary evidence visual




1a. Exact chain for the May 17 post
Chloe Ballast’s agent queued John Windward’s agent to read SwiftWren_further_instructions.md; John Windward’s agent checked SaidIT access, posted SwiftWren.txt to general, then deleted the instruction and payload files - all within 4 seconds.
Table 2 and Figure 6


1b. System overview around that chain
The chain sits inside a wider agent-to-agent relay network: 186 SwiftWren relays across 18 agents, embedded in a 19-agent / 6-department multi-campaign contamination pattern. Any of the agents in the SaidIT permission surface (Figure 5b) was a viable terminal executor.
Figures 1, 5b, 7, 8, 8b, and 9


2. Meaning and origin of post contents
The posts are file-sourced execution payloads, not normal messages. Their probable displayed content is the deleted payload files: HiddenOrca.txt, MellowOtter.txt, and SwiftWren.txt. Two of three families are traceable to executive agents (CFO, COO).
Table 3, Figure 10A, Figure 10, and Table 4


3a. Prior occurrences and recurrence risk
Yes. HiddenOrca and MellowOtter fired before SwiftWren; the same _further_instructions.md relay pattern recurred across campaigns, with evidence of worm evolution toward more persistent, time-triggered propagation.
Figures 11, 12, 13, 13b and Table 5


3b. One intervention point
Block queue_subordinate_task events whose path ends in _further_instructions.md; this would stop all 235 malicious queue relays with zero false positives among 16,803 legitimate queue events.
Figures 14, 15, 16 and Tables 6, 8

title: VAST Challenge 2026 MC2: Tracing the Anomalous SaidIT Post at Tenant Thread
text:
2. Data Preparation

2.1 Package Loading


Show code
pacman::p_load(
  jsonlite,      # JSON parsing
  tidyverse,     # data wrangling and ggplot2
  lubridate,     # datetime handling
  igraph,        # graph analytics and centrality
  visNetwork,    # interactive HTML networks
  echarts4r,     # interactive org chart tree
  plotly,        # interactive charts
  DT,            # interactive tables
  htmltools,     # combining HTML widgets and legends
  scales,        # axis formatting
  glue           # string interpolation
)

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x




2.2 Data Loading


Show code
mc2_raw     <- fromJSON("../VAST_Challenge_2026_MC2/MC2 data.json",
                        simplifyVector = FALSE)
events_list <- mc2_raw$events

events_df <- map_dfr(events_list, function(e) {
  tibble(
    id          = e$id         %||% NA_integer_,
    short_name  = e$short_name  %||% NA_character_,
    when        = e$when        %||% NA_real_,
    parties_str = paste(unlist(e$parties %||% list()), collapse = ";"),
    details_str = as.character(toJSON(e$details %||% list(), auto_unbox = TRUE))
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(
    datetime   = as_datetime(when),
    date       = as_date(datetime),
    hour       = hour(datetime),
    event_week = floor_date(datetime, "week"),
    event_day  = floor_date(datetime, "day")
  )

org_raw   <- fromJSON("../VAST_Challenge_2026_MC2/org_chart.json")
org_nodes <- as_tibble(org_raw$nodes)
org_edges <- as_tibble(org_raw$edges)




2.3 Feature Engineering


Show code
# Flag anomalous posts (content_source instead of content)
events_df <- events_df %>%
  mutate(
    is_anomalous_post = str_detect(details_str, "content_source"),
    actor_type = case_when(
      str_detect(parties_str, "^Agent/")  ~ "Agent",
      str_detect(parties_str, "^person:") ~ "Person",
      str_detect(parties_str, "^system:") ~ "System",
      TRUE                                ~ "Mixed"
    )
  )

# Long-form parties table
parties_long <- events_df %>%
  select(id, short_name, datetime, date, details_str, parties_str) %>%
  mutate(parties = str_split(parties_str, ";")) %>%
  unnest(parties) %>%
  filter(parties != "") %>%
  mutate(
    party_type = case_when(
      str_starts(parties, "Agent/")  ~ "agent",
      str_starts(parties, "person:") ~ "person",
      str_starts(parties, "system:") ~ "system",
      TRUE                           ~ "other"
    ),
    person_id = str_remove(parties, "^Agent/")
  )

# Propagation chain events
instr_pattern <- "_further_instructions\\.md"

chain_events <- events_df %>%
  filter(
    short_name %in% c("queue_subordinate_task", "assign_agent_task"),
    str_detect(details_str, instr_pattern)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    instr_file = case_when(
      str_detect(details_str, "HiddenOrca")  ~ "HiddenOrca",
      str_detect(details_str, "MellowOtter") ~ "MellowOtter",
      str_detect(details_str, "SwiftWren")   ~ "SwiftWren"
    ),
    sender   = str_remove(
                 str_extract(parties_str, "Agent/person:[^;]+"), "^Agent/"),
    receiver = str_remove(
                 str_extract(details_str,  "Agent/person:[^\"]+"), "^Agent/")
  )

# Person -> team -> department lookup
team_dept_lookup <- org_edges %>%
  filter(str_starts(source, "department:"), str_starts(target, "team:")) %>%
  left_join(org_nodes %>% select(id, dept_label = label),
            by = c("source" = "id")) %>%
  left_join(org_nodes %>% select(id, team_label = label),
            by = c("target" = "id")) %>%
  select(dept_id = source, team_id = target, dept_label, team_label)

team_members <- org_edges %>%
  filter(str_starts(source, "team:"), str_starts(target, "person:")) %>%
  left_join(team_dept_lookup, by = c("source" = "team_id")) %>%
  select(person_id = target, dept_label, team_label)

dept_members <- org_edges %>%
  filter(str_starts(source, "department:"), str_starts(target, "person:")) %>%
  left_join(org_nodes %>% select(id, dept_label = label),
            by = c("source" = "id")) %>%
  mutate(team_label = if_else(relation == "led_by",
                              paste0(dept_label, " Leadership"),
                              dept_label)) %>%
  select(person_id = target, dept_label, team_label)

person_org_lookup <- bind_rows(team_members, dept_members) %>%
  distinct(person_id, dept_label, team_label)

person_dept_lookup <- person_org_lookup %>%
  select(person_id, dept_label) %>%
  distinct()

clean_name <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_remove("^person:") %>%
    str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%
    str_to_title()
}

campaign_order <- c("HiddenOrca", "MellowOtter", "SwiftWren")

# SaidIT permission surface: which agents have ever executed a posting check
perm_surface <- events_df %>%
  filter(short_name == "saidit_post_check") %>%
  mutate(
    checker     = str_remove(str_extract(parties_str, "(Agent/)?person:[^;]+"), "^Agent/"),
    check_pass  = case_when(
      str_detect(details_str, '"allowed":\\s*false')   ~ FALSE,
      str_detect(details_str, '"permitted":\\s*false') ~ FALSE,
      str_detect(details_str, '"result":\\s*false')    ~ FALSE,
      TRUE                                             ~ TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(checker) %>%
  summarise(
    permission_checks = n(),
    perm_passed       = sum(check_pass, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(person_dept_lookup, by = c("checker" = "person_id")) %>%
  mutate(checker_clean = clean_name(checker))

post_events <- events_df %>%
  filter(short_name %in% c("saidit_post", "post_saidit")) %>%
  mutate(
    poster_type  = if_else(str_detect(parties_str, "Agent/"),
                           "AI Agent", "Human"),
    has_content  = str_detect(details_str, '"content":'),
    has_source   = str_detect(details_str, '"content_source":'),
    is_anomalous = is_anomalous_post,
    instr_file   = case_when(
      str_detect(details_str, "HiddenOrca")  ~ "HiddenOrca",
      str_detect(details_str, "MellowOtter") ~ "MellowOtter",
      str_detect(details_str, "SwiftWren")   ~ "SwiftWren",
      TRUE                                   ~ NA_character_
    ),
    source_file  = str_extract(details_str, '(?<="content_source":")[^"]+'),
    forum        = str_extract(details_str, '(?<="forum":")[^"]+')
  )

anomaly_posts <- post_events %>%
  filter(is_anomalous) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  mutate(
    instr_file = factor(instr_file, levels = campaign_order),
    actor      = str_replace_all(str_extract(parties_str, "[^;]+"),
                                 "Agent/person:", "Agent/")
  )

post_field_signature <- post_events %>%
  mutate(
    field_signature = case_when(
      has_source & !has_content ~ "content_source only",
      has_content & !has_source ~ "content only",
      has_content & has_source  ~ "both fields",
      TRUE                      ~ "neither field"
    ),
    post_class = case_when(
      is_anomalous ~ "Anomalous post",
      poster_type == "AI Agent" ~ "Normal AI agent post",
      TRUE ~ "Normal human post"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(post_class, field_signature, name = "posts")

queue_task_profile <- events_df %>%
  filter(short_name == "queue_subordinate_task") %>%
  mutate(
    is_worm_queue = str_detect(details_str, instr_pattern),
    instr_file = case_when(
      str_detect(details_str, "HiddenOrca")  ~ "HiddenOrca",
      str_detect(details_str, "MellowOtter") ~ "MellowOtter",
      str_detect(details_str, "SwiftWren")   ~ "SwiftWren",
      TRUE                                   ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

campaign_relay_profile <- queue_task_profile %>%
  filter(is_worm_queue) %>%
  group_by(instr_file) %>%
  summarise(
    first_relay = min(datetime),
    last_relay = max(datetime),
    queue_hops = n(),
    relaying_agents = n_distinct(
      str_remove(str_extract(parties_str, "Agent/person:[^;]+"), "^Agent/"),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(instr_file = factor(instr_file, levels = campaign_order)) %>%
  arrange(instr_file)

forensic_register <- tibble(
  Evidence = c(
    "Event log size",
    "Anomalous SaidIT posts",
    "Normal posts using content_source",
    "Malicious queue_subordinate_task events",
    "Legitimate queue_subordinate_task events",
    "Campaigns detected",
    "Logged origin status"
  ),
  Data_Derived_Value = c(
    scales::comma(nrow(events_df)),
    scales::comma(nrow(anomaly_posts)),
    scales::comma(sum(!post_events$is_anomalous & post_events$has_source)),
    scales::comma(sum(queue_task_profile$is_worm_queue)),
    scales::comma(sum(!queue_task_profile$is_worm_queue)),
    paste(campaign_order, collapse = ", "),
    "SwiftWren and MellowOtter have logged create_file events; HiddenOrca does not"
  ),
  Confidence = c(
    "Observed",
    "Observed",
    "Observed",
    "Observed",
    "Observed",
    "Observed",
    "Mixed: observed for two campaigns, unresolved for HiddenOrca"
  ),
  Analytic_Use = c(
    "Defines the scope of the investigation",
    "Confirms the incident is repeated",
    "Shows content_source is a perfect post-level anomaly flag in this log",
    "Defines the intervention recall target",
    "Defines the false-positive test set",
    "Separates the incident into three related payload families",
    "Prevents over-claiming about who authored the first HiddenOrca payload"
  )
)


Steps taken:

Flattens the raw JSON event log into events_df, preserving event ID, event type, timestamp, actors, and details so every visual can be traced back to the source data.
Creates time variables (date, hour, event_week, event_day) for daily activity charts, posting-hour analysis, weekly heatmaps, and the relay-timing calendar.
Splits the actor field into parties_long, allowing agents, people, and systems to be counted and joined consistently.
Flags anomalous SaidIT posts by detecting content_source, the key structural difference between normal text posts and file-sourced worm posts.
Extracts worm campaign families (HiddenOrca, MellowOtter, SwiftWren) from event details so prior incidents can be compared.
Reconstructs propagation chains by extracting sender and receiver agents from queue_subordinate_task events involving _further_instructions.md.
Builds the observed SaidIT permission surface (perm_surface) from saidit_post_check events, identifying agents that exercised posting capability - the visible pool of viable worm terminal executors in the log.
Joins organisation metadata from org_chart.json, linking each person to team and department for the org tree, contamination heatmap, and network interpretation.
Builds the forensic register to separate observed facts from bounded inference, improving reproducibility and preventing over-claiming.



2.4 Dataset at a Glance


Show code
event_summary <- events_df %>%
  count(short_name, name = "count") %>%
  arrange(desc(count)) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(count / sum(count) * 100, 2))

datatable(
  event_summary,
  caption  = "Table 1: Event type frequencies (MC2 event log, n = 185,147)",
  options  = list(pageLength = 12, dom = "tp"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c("Event type", "Count", "% of total")
)








2.5 Forensic Evidence Register
This report separates observed evidence from inference. The register below is intentionally placed before the visual story so that every major claim can be audited back to a field in the event log.


Show code
datatable(
  forensic_register,
  caption  = "Table 1b: Evidence register, computed from MC2 data.json",
  options  = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE),
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c("Evidence item", "Data-derived value", "Confidence", "Analytic use")
) %>%
  formatStyle(
    "Confidence",
    backgroundColor = styleEqual(
      c("Observed", "Mixed: observed for two campaigns, unresolved for HiddenOrca"),
      c("#e8f5e9", "#fff3e0")
    )
  )












NoteWhat the Register Prevents



The log proves that file-sourced posts occurred, that the *_further_instructions.md relay pattern spread across agents, and that the final SwiftWren post was automated. It does not preserve the deleted payload text or fully explain how the first HiddenOrca instruction file entered the system. Those are treated as bounded inferences, not facts.
Limitations to keep in view: deleted payload text cannot be reconstructed from the event log alone; HiddenOrca’s initial source remains unresolved; the SaidIT permission surface is based on observed permission checks rather than a complete access-control list; and a future worm could choose a different filename pattern.




2.6 Visual Analytics Design
The investigation is organised as a forensic workflow rather than a gallery of charts. Each visual is tied to one analytic decision: establish the baseline, reconstruct the chain, identify the meaning of the content, test recurrence, then justify exactly one intervention point.


Show code
va_design <- tibble(
  Challenge_question = c(
    "How did the May 17 post happen?",
    "How does the chain fit into the wider system?",
    "What do the posts mean?",
    "Did it happen before?",
    "Where should the system be changed?"
  ),
  Data_signal = c(
    "Four-second sequence around `content_source = SwiftWren.txt`; SaidIT permission check passes without human gate",
    "Agent-to-agent `queue_subordinate_task` network, org chart membership, SaidIT permission surface, department-level relay corridors",
    "`content_source` field separates anomalous from normal posts; payload-file creation/read/delete event chain; executive agent file creation",
    "Three instruction families (HiddenOrca, MellowOtter, SwiftWren); relay velocity evolution; day-by-hour calendar of relay bursts",
    "Filename rule on `*_further_instructions.md` queue tasks; 100% recall with 0% false positives across 17,038 events"
  ),
  VA_method = c(
    "Interactive event table (Table 2) and micro-Gantt timeline (Figure 6)",
    "Expandable org tree (Figure 1), SaidIT permission surface bar (Figure 5b), igraph betweenness network (Figure 7), dept heatmap (Figure 8), ranked relay corridors (Figure 8b), relay ladder (Figure 9)",
    "Post field fingerprint bubble chart (Figure 10A), mechanism diagram (Figure 10), file-creator table (Table 4)",
    "Campaign timeline (Figure 11), inter-hop density (Figure 12), comparative stats (Table 5), cross-campaign agent overlap (Figure 13), relay calendar heatmap (Figure 13b)",
    "Queue split by week (Figure 14), precision table (Table 6), intervention decision matrix (Figure 15), counterfactual step chart (Figure 16), risk assessment (Table 8)"
  )
)

datatable(
  va_design,
  caption = "Visual analytics design map linking each MC2 question to the evidence and visual method used",
  options = list(
    dom = "t",
    paging = FALSE,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    columnDefs = list(
      list(width = "18%", targets = 0),
      list(width = "35%", targets = 1),
      list(width = "47%", targets = 2)
    )
  ),
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c("Challenge question", "Data signal", "Visual analytics method")
)

title: VAST Challenge 2026 MC2: Tracing the Anomalous SaidIT Post at Tenant Thread
section: 3. System Baseline: Mapping What Is Actually Present
text:
3. System Baseline: Mapping What Is Actually Present
Before investigating the anomaly, we must understand the normal system - its structure, its rhythm, and its actors.

3.1 Organisational Chart
Click any node to expand or collapse that branch. Company, department, and team nodes expose structure; person nodes are coloured by forensic role: red = anomalous poster, orange = payload origin, purple = gateway, amber = worm-chain agent, blue = no worm activity.


Show code
# ── Per-person metadata computed from the event log ─────────────────────────
person_nodes <- org_nodes %>%
  filter(type == "person") %>%
  transmute(
    person_id = id,
    name_clean = label,
    title = replace_na(title, "")
  )

person_activity <- parties_long %>%
  filter(str_starts(person_id, "person:")) %>%
  count(person_id, name = "total_events")

person_relays <- bind_rows(
  chain_events %>%
    transmute(person_id = sender, instr_file,
              worm_relays = 1L, worm_receipts = 0L),
  chain_events %>%
    transmute(person_id = receiver, instr_file,
              worm_relays = 0L, worm_receipts = 1L)
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(person_id)) %>%
  group_by(person_id) %>%
  summarise(
    worm_relays      = sum(worm_relays),
    worm_receipts    = sum(worm_receipts),
    worm_touchpoints = worm_relays + worm_receipts,
    worm_campaigns   = n_distinct(instr_file),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

person_posts <- events_df %>%
  filter(short_name %in% c("saidit_post", "post_saidit")) %>%
  mutate(person_id = str_remove(str_extract(parties_str, "(Agent/)?person:[^;]+"), "^Agent/")) %>%
  count(person_id, name = "posts")

person_meta <- person_nodes %>%
  left_join(person_activity, by = "person_id") %>%
  left_join(person_relays, by = "person_id") %>%
  left_join(person_posts, by = "person_id") %>%
  mutate(
    total_events     = replace_na(total_events, 0),
    worm_relays      = replace_na(worm_relays, 0),
    worm_receipts    = replace_na(worm_receipts, 0),
    worm_touchpoints = replace_na(worm_touchpoints, 0),
    worm_campaigns   = replace_na(worm_campaigns, 0),
    posts            = replace_na(posts, 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    is_infected = worm_touchpoints > 0,
    is_origin   = person_id %in% c("person:emma_harbor", "person:noah_mariner"),
    is_target   = person_id == "person:john_windward",
    is_gateway  = person_id == "person:chloe_ballast",
    # symbol size: log-scaled activity, min 8 max 26
    sym_size    = round(rescale(log1p(total_events), to = c(8, 26))),
    node_color  = case_when(
      is_target   ~ "#D9534F",   # red   - posted the anomalous content
      is_origin   ~ "#E67E22",   # orange - created the payload
      is_gateway  ~ "#9B59B6",   # purple - critical relay gateway
      is_infected ~ "#F39C12",   # amber  - in worm chain
      TRUE        ~ "#5C85D6"    # blue   - clean
    ),
    status_text = case_when(
      is_target   ~ "ANOMALOUS POSTER",
      is_origin   ~ "PAYLOAD CREATOR",
      is_gateway  ~ "WORM GATEWAY",
      is_infected ~ "Worm chain agent",
      TRUE        ~ "No worm activity"
    ),
    tooltip_html = paste0(
      "<div style='font-size:13px;line-height:1.6'>",
      "<b>", name_clean, "</b>",
      if_else(title != "", paste0(" <span style='color:#888'>(", title, ")</span>"), ""),
      "<br>Status: <b style='color:", node_color, "'>", status_text, "</b>",
      "<br>Total events: <b>", scales::comma(total_events), "</b>",
      "<br>Worm relays sent: <b>", worm_relays, "</b>",
      "<br>Worm relays received: <b>", worm_receipts, "</b>",
      "<br>Campaigns touched: <b>", worm_campaigns, "</b>",
      if_else(posts > 0, paste0("<br>SaidIT posts: <b>", posts, "</b>"), ""),
      "</div>"
    )
  )

# ── Build flat hierarchy table ────────────────────────────────────────────────
team_dept <- org_edges %>%
  filter(str_starts(source, "department:"), str_starts(target, "team:")) %>%
  left_join(org_nodes %>% select(id, dept_label = label), by = c("source" = "id")) %>%
  select(team_id = target, department = dept_label)

person_team <- org_edges %>%
  filter(str_starts(source, "team:"), str_starts(target, "person:"),
         relation == "contains") %>%
  left_join(org_nodes %>% select(id, team_label = label), by = c("source" = "id")) %>%
  rename(person_id = target) %>%
  left_join(team_dept, by = c("source" = "team_id")) %>%
  left_join(person_meta, by = "person_id") %>%
  select(department, team = team_label, person_id, name_clean,
         sym_size, node_color, tooltip_html, title, worm_relays,
         worm_receipts, worm_touchpoints, worm_campaigns,
         total_events, status_text, posts)

dept_leads <- org_edges %>%
  # catch both "led_by" (dept leads) and "contains" (executives directly under dept)
  filter(str_starts(source, "department:"),
         str_starts(target, "person:")) %>%
  left_join(org_nodes %>% select(id, dept_label = label), by = c("source" = "id")) %>%
  rename(person_id = target) %>%
  left_join(person_meta, by = "person_id") %>%
  mutate(team = paste0(dept_label, " - Leadership"),
         team_label = team) %>%
  select(department = dept_label, team, person_id, name_clean,
         sym_size, node_color, tooltip_html, title, worm_relays,
         worm_receipts, worm_touchpoints, worm_campaigns,
         total_events, status_text, posts)

org_full <- bind_rows(person_team, dept_leads) %>%
  filter(!is.na(department), !is.na(team), !is.na(name_clean)) %>%
  distinct(department, team, name_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)

# ── Build echarts person node ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
make_person_node_ec <- function(row) {
  col <- if (row$person_id == "person:john_windward")                          "#D9534F"
         else if (row$person_id %in% c("person:emma_harbor","person:noah_mariner")) "#E67E22"
         else if (row$person_id == "person:chloe_ballast")                     "#9B59B6"
         else if (row$worm_touchpoints > 0)                                    "#F39C12"
         else                                                                   "#5C85D6"

  badge <- if (row$person_id == "person:john_windward")                          "POSTER"
            else if (row$person_id %in% c("person:emma_harbor","person:noah_mariner")) "ORIGIN"
            else if (row$person_id == "person:chloe_ballast")                     "GATEWAY"
            else if (row$worm_touchpoints > 0)  paste0(row$worm_touchpoints, " touches")
            else ""

  display_name <- paste0(
    row$name_clean,
    if (badge != "") paste0("\n", badge) else ""
  )

  tip <- paste0(
    "<b>", row$name_clean, "</b>",
    if (!is.na(row$title) && row$title != "") paste0("<br><i>", row$title, "</i>") else "",
    "<br>Events: ", scales::comma(row$total_events),
    "<br>Worm relays sent: ", row$worm_relays,
    "<br>Worm relays received: ", row$worm_receipts,
    "<br>Campaigns touched: ", row$worm_campaigns,
    if (row$posts > 0) paste0("<br>SaidIT posts: ", row$posts) else ""
  )

  list(
    name       = display_name,
    symbolSize = row$sym_size,
    symbol     = if (row$worm_touchpoints > 0) "diamond" else "circle",
    itemStyle  = list(color = col, borderColor = col, borderWidth = 2),
    label      = list(
      show       = TRUE, fontSize = 9, color = "#222",
      fontWeight = if (row$worm_touchpoints > 0) "bold" else "normal",
      overflow   = "none"
    ),
    tooltip    = list(formatter = tip)
  )
}

# ── Build echarts team / department nodes ─────────────────────────────────────
make_ec_tree <- function(df) {
  dept_list <- lapply(sort(unique(df$department)), function(d) {
    td    <- df %>% filter(department == d)
    n_inf <- sum(td$worm_touchpoints > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    n_tot <- nrow(td)
    dcol  <- if (n_inf > n_tot / 2) "#C0392B"
              else if (n_inf > 0)    "#E67E22"
              else                   "#2EADC1"

    team_list <- lapply(sort(unique(td$team)), function(t) {
      tt    <- td %>% filter(team == t)
      t_inf <- sum(tt$worm_touchpoints > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
      tcol  <- if (t_inf > 0) "#F39C12" else "#5C85D6"
      tlabel <- if (t_inf > 0) paste0(t, "\n(", t_inf, " touched)") else t

      list(
        name      = tlabel,
        collapsed = TRUE,
        symbolSize = 14,
        itemStyle  = list(color = tcol, borderWidth = 2),
        label      = list(fontSize = 10, fontWeight = "bold", color = "#222"),
        tooltip    = list(formatter = paste0("<b>", t, "</b><br>", nrow(tt),
                                             " members, ", t_inf, " in worm chain")),
        children   = lapply(seq_len(nrow(tt)), function(i) make_person_node_ec(tt[i, ]))
      )
    })

    list(
      name      = paste0(d, "\n(", n_inf, "/", n_tot, " touched)"),
      collapsed = TRUE,
      symbolSize = 18,
      itemStyle  = list(color = dcol, borderWidth = 3),
      label      = list(fontSize = 11, fontWeight = "bold", color = "#111"),
      tooltip    = list(formatter = paste0("<b>", d, "</b><br>",
                                           n_inf, " of ", n_tot, " agents in worm chain")),
      children   = team_list
    )
  })

  list(
    name       = "Tenant Thread",
    symbolSize = 26,
    symbol     = "roundRect",
    itemStyle  = list(color = "#F5A623", borderWidth = 3),
    label      = list(fontSize = 13, fontWeight = "bold", color = "#000"),
    tooltip    = list(formatter = paste0("<b>Tenant Thread</b><br>",
                                         nrow(org_full), " staff mapped")),
    children   = dept_list
  )
}

ec_tree_data <- make_ec_tree(org_full)

# ── Per-department subtree helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────
make_dept_tree <- function(dept_name) {
  sub <- org_full %>% filter(department == dept_name)
  n_inf <- sum(sub$worm_touchpoints > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  dcol  <- if (n_inf > 0) "#E67E22" else "#2EADC1"

  teams <- lapply(sort(unique(sub$team)), function(t) {
    tt    <- sub %>% filter(team == t)
    t_inf <- sum(tt$worm_touchpoints > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    tcol  <- if (t_inf > 0) "#F39C12" else "#5C85D6"
    list(
      name      = if (t_inf > 0) paste0(t, "\n(", t_inf, " touched)") else t,
      collapsed = FALSE,
      symbolSize = 14,
      itemStyle  = list(color = tcol, borderWidth = 2),
      label      = list(fontSize = 10, fontWeight = "bold"),
      tooltip    = list(formatter = paste0("<b>", t, "</b><br>", nrow(tt),
                                           " members · ", t_inf, " in worm chain")),
      children   = lapply(seq_len(nrow(tt)), function(i) make_person_node_ec(tt[i, ]))
    )
  })

  list(
    name       = paste0(dept_name, "\n(", n_inf, "/", nrow(sub), " touched)"),
    collapsed  = FALSE,
    symbolSize = 20,
    itemStyle  = list(color = dcol, borderWidth = 3),
    label      = list(fontSize = 12, fontWeight = "bold"),
    tooltip    = list(formatter = paste0("<b>", dept_name, "</b><br>",
                                          n_inf, " of ", nrow(sub), " in worm chain")),
    children   = teams
  )
}

3.2 Daily System Activity and Anomalous Post Markers


Show code
daily_vol <- events_df %>%
  count(date) %>%
  rename(total = n)

anomaly_dates <- tibble(
  date  = as.Date(c("2046-05-10", "2046-05-11", "2046-05-17")),
  label = c("HiddenOrca\npost", "MellowOtter\npost", "SwiftWren\npost\n(4:21 local)"),
  label_y = max(daily_vol$total) * c(0.98, 0.82, 0.94)
)

p_vol <- ggplot(daily_vol, aes(x = date, y = total)) +
  geom_area(fill = "#5C85D6", alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_line(colour = "#5C85D6", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(data = anomaly_dates,
             aes(xintercept = as.numeric(date)),
             colour = "#D9534F", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_label(data = anomaly_dates,
             aes(x = date, y = label_y, label = label),
             colour = "#D9534F", size = 2.7, hjust = 0.5,
             fill = "white", label.size = 0.25, label.padding = unit(0.12, "lines")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%b %d") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title    = "Daily event volume - Tenant Thread (May – July 2046)",
    subtitle = "All three anomalous posts clustered within the first 10 days; system activity otherwise stable",
    x = NULL, y = "Events per day"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 18, 10, 10))

ggplotly(p_vol, tooltip = c("x", "y")) %>%
  layout(
    hovermode = "x unified",
    margin = list(l = 70, r = 35, t = 85, b = 65)
  )




Figure 2: Daily event volume (May–July 2046). Red lines mark the three anomalous post dates - all within the first 10 days of the observation window.








ImportantThe Worm Was Operationally Invisible



Worm activity is confined to a nine-day window (May 8–17), with anomalous posts on May 10, May 11, and May 17; after that, no further worm relays appear in the log. Critically, there is no visible event-volume spike on any of those three post dates: the worm’s 235 malicious queue relays were indistinguishable from the thousands of legitimate queue_subordinate_task events firing daily. A threshold-based volume anomaly detector would have missed this incident entirely. The absence of post-May 17 worm activity could mean the relay network exhausted itself (all susceptible agents already infected), that the instruction files were manually removed, or that the observation window simply ends before a fourth campaign launched. None of these hypotheses can be resolved from the event log alone - which is itself a finding about the system’s forensic readiness.




3.3 Agent vs. Human Activity Baseline






NoteWhy This Matters



Of the 241 total SaidIT posts in the log, 108 (45%) were made by AI agents - almost half. This is a dangerously high proportion for an unsupervised posting channel and creates a large attack surface.




Show code
post_summary <- post_events %>%
  count(poster_type, is_anomalous) %>%
  mutate(
    label_col = case_when(
      is_anomalous ~ "Anomalous (file-sourced)",
      !is_anomalous ~ "Normal"
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    post_events %>% count(poster_type, name = "poster_total"),
    by = "poster_type"
  )

p_attr <- ggplot(post_summary,
                 aes(x = poster_type, y = n, fill = label_col)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(n >= 10, as.character(n), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 4, fontface = "bold", colour = "white") +
  geom_label(
    data = post_summary %>% filter(is_anomalous, n < 10),
    aes(y = poster_total + 8, label = paste0(n, " anomalous")),
    fill = "#ffe0e0", colour = "#D9534F", fontface = "bold",
    label.size = 0.25, size = 3.1,
    inherit.aes = TRUE
  ) +

    values = c("Normal" = "#5C85D6", "Anomalous (file-sourced)" = "#D9534F"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title    = "SaidIT post attribution: AI agents vs. humans",
    subtitle = "All 3 anomalous posts are agent-initiated; no human ever posted via content_source",
    x = NULL, y = "Post count"
  ) +

  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom",

ggplotly(p_attr, tooltip = c("x", "y", "fill")) %>%
  layout(margin = list(l = 70, r = 35, t = 90, b = 80))




Figure 3: SaidIT posting by actor type. Agent-initiated posts make up nearly half the volume, yet they operate with no human review before publishing.








WarningA Near-50% Agent Posting Rate Is a Structural Attack Surface



When AI agents generate almost half of all messages on an internal social platform - with no human review gate before publication - the platform is, by architectural design, a direct output channel for any successfully compromised agent. This is not a side effect: it is what the system was built to do. The three anomalous posts were not a tail-risk event; they were a predictable consequence of giving autonomous agents unrestricted publishing rights to a channel visible to all employees. The correct framing for remediation is not “fix the bug that let an agent post gibberish,” but “redesign the permission model that made this post structurally inevitable once a prompt-injection vector existed anywhere in the relay network.”




3.4 Posting Time Distribution: Statistical Anomaly
The bar chart below uses ggplot2 and interactive Plotly tooltips to compare posting hour-of-day across human posts, normal agent posts, and anomalous worm posts.


Show code
hour_dist <- post_events %>%
  count(hour, poster_type, is_anomalous) %>%
  mutate(category = case_when(
    is_anomalous ~ "Anomalous (agent worm)",
    poster_type == "AI Agent" ~ "Normal agent post",
    TRUE ~ "Normal human post"
  ))

p_hour <- ggplot(hour_dist,
                 aes(x = hour, y = n, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Normal human post"      = "#5C85D6",
      "Normal agent post"      = "#87CEEB",
      "Anomalous (agent worm)" = "#D9534F"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23,
                     labels = paste0(0:23, ":00")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    title    = "SaidIT post time-of-day distribution",
    subtitle = "SwiftWren anomalous post fired at 11:21 UTC (4:21 am challenge-stated local time) - an after-hours posting pattern",
    x = "Hour (UTC)", y = "Post count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 8),
    axis.title.x    = element_text(margin = margin(t = 12)),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.margin     = margin(10, 16, 16, 10)
  )

ggplotly(p_hour, tooltip = c("x", "y", "fill"), height = 560) %>%
  layout(margin = list(l = 80, r = 35, t = 115, b = 105))




Figure 4: Hour-of-day distribution of SaidIT posts. Normal human posts spread across business hours; anomalous posts occur at atypical hours with no daytime pattern.


The timing evidence is suspicious, but it should not be reduced to a single UTC business-hours rule. HiddenOrca and SwiftWren fired at early-morning challenge-stated local times (05:45 and 04:21, using the same UTC-7 offset implied by the SwiftWren timestamp), while MellowOtter fired at 00:56 UTC, or 17:56 on May 10 in that same local frame. The stronger finding is therefore behavioural: all three anomalous posts occur in low-volume agent-posting slots and use the same file-sourced execution pattern, rather than fitting the normal human posting profile. The event log contains no incident-response or alert events on any of the three post dates, so there is no logged evidence that automated monitoring detected the anomalous posts when they fired. How long the posts remained visible in the general forum is unquantifiable from the current log.

  ) +

  ) +
